- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods; reduce forecast peaks when sentiment is high or trending upward.
- Underestimate prices in bearish sentiment periods; raise forecasts when sentiment is low or trending downward.
- Lagged price movements are often over-predicted; model should adjust for recent momentum by smoothing out short-term spikes.
- Overshoots after sharp price spikes (especially in bullish sentiment) should be capped or dampened to avoid overcorrection.
- Mean reversion is stronger in high volatility periods; model should incorporate sentiment-driven reversion bias when sentiment is extreme.
- Forecast horizon 30d tends to overestimate upward trends in early periods; reduce forecast slope when sentiment is rising sharply.
- When sentiment is neutral or mixed, forecasts should be conservative; avoid large deviations from recent 18-day average unless sentiment strongly shifts.
